name: Iraq

campaign_state.basis: Attacks on energy facilities in Iraq are reported from 2022 onward, including in 2026. No end is reported.
campaign_state.limitation: One status search per system, in English, on the date checked. A search that returns no recent report does not show that none occurred.

no_index_reason: No index is published for this country. The Monitored-Area ESDI's sector weights, decay horizons and transmission measure were built for a strike campaign and do not transfer (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §1-§3). This view shows reported major disruptions and energy-system context instead.

sectors.label: Refining

sectors.reason: No current plant list was read, and installed capacity is not stated in the source used. The federal grid and the Kurdistan Region are reported separately. Shortage is the normal state of the system, so capacity would not measure service.
sectors.label: Electric generation

sectors.reason: No regional inventory, and none is sought: grid mapping is out of scope. The event-burden measure does not fit.
sectors.label: Transmission burden

sectors.reason: No public capacity inventory was read, and building one would centre on export routing, which is out of scope. The ESDI's refining-base proxy does not fit a crude exporter.
sectors.label: Oil logistics & export

sectors.reason: National production, flaring and import figures only; no processing inventory was read. LNG and gas storage are not yet researched.
sectors.label: Gas

sectors.reason: Not applicable: EIA's energy table for Iraq marks coal as not applicable, and no coal plant appears in any source read. The sector does not exist here, which is different from unknown.
sectors.label: Coal

reporting_environment_text: Disruption is disclosed mainly through company and ministry statements, usually only when material to investors or the state.
reporting_note: The federal oil and electricity ministries, state companies and the Kurdistan Region's ministries issue statements after large events. There is no event register, and official sites refuse automated reading, so statements are read as carried by news agencies and regional media. The coverage of this record cannot be computed.
comparability_statement: Each country is measured on its own terms. Event counts reflect what is publicly reported under that country's reporting rules, not how often disruption happens. A country with fewer recorded events is not shown to be safer, more resilient or less disrupted. Figures are not comparable across countries and are never ranked.

geography.note: Iraq has 19 governorates in law since 2025, when Halabja became the nineteenth; Natural Earth draws 18, with Halabja inside As-Sulaymaniyah. The Kurdistan Region is a federal region of Iraq that contains governorates (Constitution, Art. 117); it is not a separate unit or system here. Events are placed by the governorate Natural Earth draws, which is an analytic choice, not a statement about the administration of any area.

rulings.note: A governorate of the Kurdistan Region, a federal region of Iraq. Shown as an Iraqi governorate. Natural Earth spells it Arbil.
A governorate of the Kurdistan Region, a federal region of Iraq. Shown as an Iraqi governorate. Natural Earth spells it Dihok.

A governorate of the Kurdistan Region, a federal region of Iraq. Natural Earth draws Halabja governorate (created by a federal law passed on 14 April 2025) inside it. An event reported in Halabja is placed here, and the record says so.

Kirkuk governorate, under Natural Earth's code and former name (At-Ta'mim); ISO is reported to list it as IQ-KI. The Constitution (Art. 140) names Kirkuk among territories whose status is to be settled by a process that has not been completed. Events are placed by the boundary Natural Earth draws.

precision_policy.reason: Attacks on energy facilities in Iraq have been reported from 2022 to this month. In the governorates where most were reported, a governorate and an infrastructure class together name one facility, and publishing some governorates but not others would show which. An attack or sabotage record is therefore recorded for the country, with no governorate, facility or operator. Other events (accidents, grid failures, fuel-supply shortfalls) are placed by governorate.

event_summary.note: Counts what was reported and found, not what occurred.

inclusion_threshold.applies_to: country systems only. Never applied to the Russia theatre corpus, which predates it and does not pass it (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.2).
inclusion_threshold.rule: A publicly reported disruption to energy infrastructure that meets at least one clause below, supported by at least one source with a URL.

clauses.1: Refinery, gas-processing plant or LNG terminal shut down, or throughput materially cut, with the effect reported.
clauses.2: Export or import terminal operations suspended.
clauses.3: Trunk pipeline shut down, or force majeure declared on it.
clauses.4: A power plant of about 500 MW or more forced offline with a reported effect, or a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages.
clauses.5: A grid event affecting about 100,000 customers or more, or a grid-operator emergency declaration.
clauses.6: A coal-mine event that materially cut supply.
clauses.7: Production shut in at a reported, material volume.

exclusions: minor unit trips with no reported effect
policy decisions and sanctions with no physical effect (for example OPEC+ quota changes)
inferences from proximity to an event (a wildfire near a facility is not a disruption of it)
known_weaknesses: Absolute thresholds (500 MW, 100,000 customers) mean very different things in systems that differ in size by thirty times; a province-wide outage in a small province can fall below them.
'With reported effect' measures how much a country discloses as well as what happened.
One storm can produce several records; episodes are not yet grouped.
See GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.1 for the full red-team.

episode_bases.named_hazard: The records name the same storm, flood, heat wave or other hazard.
episode_bases.explicit_common_event: A source explicitly says these records belong to one common event.
episode_bases.coordinated_wave: A source explicitly identifies these records as one coordinated attack or wave.
episode_bases.explicit_continuation: A later record reports the same operational disruption continuing.
episode_bases.singleton: No other record is tied to this one by a named hazard or an explicit common event.

review_summary.note: Blind reviewed (since iteration 17): three independent reviewers, none of whom saw the researcher's reasoning or each other, checked the evidence, the safety of the wording and the classification; all three accepted it. Dual reviewed: a researcher found the record and a second, independent reviewer opened its sources. Legacy: published before independent review was required, checked by one reviewer against the threshold and the scope scan; these are grandfathered by id and leave the list as they are re-reviewed.

release_rule.text: Facility-specific restart, recovery or operating status for a record in a campaign is published only once the campaign is recorded as ended and 30 days have passed. While it is active the event itself is published; its facility status is not.

profile.as_of_note: Compiled 2026-11-11 by the Iraq source-audit lane. CONTEXT ONLY: never a scoring input. Every value was read on the cited page in this session through a text rendering of the page; mixed vintages (2023-2026) are stated per row and must not be combined into one 'current' picture. Bases differ by row: several are EIA estimates, the electricity rows cover Federal Iraq only (the Kurdistan Region is reported separately), and installed generating capacity is NOT stated in the source, so no generating_capacity row is given. OPEC, IEA, Energy Institute and the Iraqi ministries' own sites refused automated access on this date, so no figure is taken from them. No facility row and no export breakdown is recorded. See docs/countries/IQ_SOURCE_AUDIT.md.

significance: Crude oil and other petroleum liquids made up 96% of Iraq's primary energy production in 2023 and natural gas 4% (EIA).
EIA puts Iraq's proved crude oil reserves at 145 billion barrels (EIA, 2025).

For 2023 EIA reports 372 billion cubic feet of natural gas produced, 625 billion cubic feet flared (a World Bank figure) and 310 billion cubic feet imported; the three figures are on different bases and are not summed (EIA).

Federal Iraq generated an estimated 150 TWh in 2023, 58% from natural gas and 41% from crude oil and petroleum; EIA estimates available peak supply at about 25 GW in 2024 against about 48 GW of peak summer demand (EIA).

research_freshness.note: Research coverage describes the event search, not the sources: a country's sources can all be current while its search is unfinished, and a finished search can rest on a source whose own data is old. A fully executed search procedure is not complete knowledge: it means the declared sources were searched, not that nothing else happened.

recovery_coverage.policy: Observed recovery, or a sourced estimate labelled as an estimate. Nothing is modelled, and an event never ages out as recovered.

source_families.note: Which kinds of source the published events cite. Shows the reporting environment; it is not a quality score.

citation_quality.link_check_note: The citations of this system have not been link-checked.

monthly.rationale: three monthly releases missed, plus a month of publication lag

semiannual.rationale: two half-yearly releases missed, plus about a month of lag

annual.rationale: one annual release missed, plus about a month of lag

event_driven.rationale: no release cycle; the registry entry (access, licence, address) is re-checked at least twice a year
